name: Myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS, adult)
theme: two goals, one honest scoreboard · the VERONA lesson

meta.title: Myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS) in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Myelodysplastic neoplasms (MDS), adult - lower-risk and higher-risk pathways
meta.population: Adults (median age at diagnosis ~71). Lower-risk disease is an anemia-and-quality-of-life problem with a growing menu (ESA, luspatercept, imetelstat, lenalidomide for del(5q)); higher-risk disease is a survival problem (azacitidine, allogeneic transplant for the fit). MPN and MDS/MPN overlap (CMML) are DIFFERENT disease families per WHO-HAEM5 - the overlap gate reroutes them out; blasts >=20% is AML by definition and reroutes to the aml trainer.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for MDS - the disease where the FIRST decision is which disease you are actually treating (risk group changes the goal itself: quality-of-life vs survival), where transfusion-independence endpoints must never masquerade as survival, and where the VERONA readout (better marrow responses, no OS benefit) is the freshest response-is-not-survival lesson in oncology.
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022): myelodysplastic neoplasms as their own family, separate from MPN and MDS/MPN; blasts >=20% defines AML
meta.response: IWG response criteria (2006, updated 2023); risk by IPSS-M (molecular, 31 genes) with IPSS-R as the non-molecular fallback

stages.label: Presentation & cytopenias
stages.question: Which cytopenia is driving the picture - and is this even MDS?
stages.decision: Characterize the cytopenias and transfusion burden; exclude reactive causes; marrow with cytogenetics and molecular panel.

stages.label: Classify & risk-stratify
stages.question: IPSS-M (or IPSS-R): lower-risk or higher-risk?
stages.decision: Compute the risk score before choosing therapy - the score changes the GOAL, not just the drug.

stages.label: Plan first-line therapy
stages.question: Lower-risk: which anemia rung? Higher-risk: azacitidine, and is transplant on the table?
stages.decision: Lower-risk: route by transfusion burden, endogenous EPO, ESA exposure, del(5q). Higher-risk: azacitidine backbone; refer the fit for donor search NOW.

stages.label: Response checkpoint
stages.question: Is the hypomethylating agent working by cycle 4-6? Did transfusion independence arrive by week 24?
stages.decision: HMA response is judged after 4-6 cycles, not 1-2; lower-risk rungs are re-routed if transfusion independence has not arrived by ~24 weeks.

stages.label: Transplant fork
stages.question: Fit, higher-risk, 50-75: has the donor search started?
stages.decision: Biologic-assignment evidence: having a matched donor identified within 90 days and proceeding to reduced-intensity transplant added 21 absolute points of 3-yea…

stages.label: HMA failure
stages.question: The azacitidine stopped working - what now?
stages.decision: No standard of care exists after HMA failure; trial-first, transplant for the (still) fit, honest numbers for everything else.

stages.label: Trial screen
stages.question: Which open randomized options exist for this profile?
stages.decision: Screen the live phase-3 menu: IDH1-mutant (PyramIDH), higher-risk frontline (GLORA-4, the post-VERONA BCL-2-family retry), lower-risk ESA-naive (elritercept vs…

stages.label: Decision artifacts
stages.question: Which results are load-bearing for this plan?
stages.decision: Molecular panel (IPSS-M), cytogenetics (del(5q)), endogenous EPO level, transfusion log, donor search status.

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: Median age at diagnosis ~71. Age was an additive survival feature in the IPSS-R analysis; it also drives the transplant-fitness conversation.
Patient.helpPatient: MDS is mostly a disease of later life. Age matters some for the numbers, and more for which options are practical.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Performance status was an additive survival feature in IPSS-R and is central to transplant fitness.
Patient.helpPatient: How much the disease limits daily activity - it shapes both the outlook and which treatments make sense.

Patient.label: Transplant fitness
Patient.help: BMT CTN 1102 enrolled 50-75-year-olds: reduced-intensity transplant fitness is a deliberate assessment, not an age cutoff.
Patient.helpPatient: Whether a donor-transplant path is medically realistic. In this disease that question is asked seriously up to the mid-70s.

Disease.label: Bone marrow blasts
Disease.help: The marrow blast percentage is a core IPSS variable and the AML boundary: >=20% is acute myeloid leukemia by definition and reroutes to the AML trainer.
Disease.helpPatient: The share of immature cells in the marrow. Above a set line the disease has a different name (AML) and its own trainer.

Disease.label: IPSS-M / IPSS-R risk group
Disease.help: The composite risk call (IPSS-M preferred; IPSS-R when the molecular panel is unavailable). It changes the treatment GOAL - ranking is withheld while it is pending. IPSS-M restratified 46% of patient…
Disease.helpPatient: The risk score result decides whether the plan is about quality of life for years, or about acting on survival soon. It is worth waiting the extra days for the gene panel.

Disease.label: del(5q)
Disease.help: The one cytogenetic lesion with its own drug: lenalidomide produced transfusion independence in 67% in the pivotal del(5q) study.
Disease.helpPatient: A specific chromosome finding that unlocks a pill with unusually strong results for the anemia.

Disease.label: RBC transfusion burden
Disease.help: The lower-risk treatment indication: the anemia rungs (ESA, luspatercept, imetelstat, lenalidomide) exist for transfusion-dependent disease; independent disease is observed.
Disease.helpPatient: Whether regular blood transfusions are already needed. If not, watching carefully is a real plan, not neglect.

Disease.label: Endogenous erythropoietin
Disease.help: COMMANDS enrolled serum EPO <500 U/L; above it, ESA-family responses are poor and the ladder skips ahead.
Disease.helpPatient: A blood test that predicts whether the body will answer erythropoietin-type shots. A high value means those shots rarely help.

Disease.label: ESA exposure
Disease.help: The lower-risk ladder's routing switch: COMMANDS (luspatercept) enrolled ESA-naive patients; IMerge (imetelstat) and its FDA label are for ESA relapsed/refractory/ineligible disease.
Disease.helpPatient: Whether the erythropoietin-type shots have already been tried. The menu is different before and after.

Disease.label: Proliferative / overlap features
Disease.help: Sustained monocytosis or dysplastic-plus-proliferative features move the diagnosis into the MDS/MPN overlap family (CMML and relatives) - a different WHO-HAEM5 family that every pivotal MDS trial exc…
Disease.helpPatient: Some marrow diseases both under-produce and over-produce cells at once. Those have their own playbook - this trainer hands them off rather than guessing.

On treatment.label: HMA response (cycle 4-6)
On treatment.help: Azacitidine is judged at cycle 4-6, not cycle 1-2 (median time to first response 2-3 cycles). Failure routes to the HMA-failure menu, where the honest cohort median is 5.6 months.
On treatment.helpPatient: This treatment is a slow burn - the marrow needs months to answer. Stopping too early is the classic mistake.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Where you are.label: Your state (optional)
Where you are.help: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.
Where you are.helpPatient: Only used to list cancer centres near you. Leave blank to see national results.

Newly diagnosed.name: Observation + supportive care (lower-risk, transfusion-independent)
Newly diagnosed.patient: Lower-risk disease that is not yet forcing transfusions: careful watching is the recommended plan, with every treatment held in reserve.

Newly diagnosed.name: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agent (epoetin alfa)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN MDS v3.2026 first anemia rung when serum EPO <500 U/L
Newly diagnosed.patient: A weekly shot that asks the marrow to make more red cells - the classic first move when the body's own erythropoietin is low.

Newly diagnosed.name: Luspatercept first-line (COMMANDS)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN MDS v3.2026; FDA frontline label per COMMANDS
Newly diagnosed.patient: A shot every three weeks that helps red cells finish maturing - in a head-to-head trial it beat the classic shot at freeing people from transfusions.

Newly diagnosed.name: Imetelstat after ESA failure (IMerge)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: grade 3-4 neutropenia and thrombocytopenia are common and label-warned; infusion reactions
Newly diagnosed.patient: For anemia that no longer answers the shots: a monthly two-hour infusion with a real chance of freedom from transfusions.

Newly diagnosed.name: Lenalidomide for del(5q)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN MDS v3.2026 for del(5q) lower-risk transfusion-dependent disease
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: moderate-to-severe neutropenia (55%) and thrombocytopenia (44%) - dose interruptions are the rule, not the exception
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the specific chromosome finding del(5q): a capsule with unusually strong odds of ending transfusions - two out of three in the pivotal study.

Newly diagnosed.name: Azacitidine (higher-risk backbone)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN MDS v3.2026 category 1 backbone for higher-risk disease
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: cytopenias (often worse in cycles 1-2), injection-site reactions, GI
Newly diagnosed.patient: The proven backbone for higher-risk disease: a week of injections each month that, in the landmark trial, meaningfully extended survival.

Newly diagnosed.name: Azacitidine + venetoclax (VERONA: no OS benefit)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: not a guideline-preferred frontline standard after VERONA; subgroup signals (TP53-wildtype, excess blasts) are hypothesis-generating only
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: adds venetoclax cytopenia depth and febrile neutropenia (23% vs 16%) to the azacitidine base
Newly diagnosed.patient: Adding the leukemia pill to the monthly injections cleans up the marrow more often - but in the big trial people did not live longer, and it adds side effects. That is why it sits where it sits on this list.

Newly diagnosed.name: Reduced-intensity allogeneic transplant (fit, higher-risk)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN MDS v3.2026: transplant evaluation at diagnosis for fit higher-risk patients
Newly diagnosed.evidence: multicenter biologic-assignment trial (donor vs no donor)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: transplant-related mortality and GVHD are real and material; the 3-year OS figure above already includes them (intention-to-treat)
Newly diagnosed.patient: The only path built for cure: a donor's immune system replaces the failing marrow. It is the hardest road here, and in the landmark study fit older patients who had a donor lived meaningfully longer - counting everything that can go wrong.

Newly diagnosed.name: Supportive care only (higher-risk)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: a legitimate, chosen path - never a default by omission
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; the disease's own cytopenias dominate
Newly diagnosed.patient: Choosing comfort and count support without disease-modifying treatment. It is a real choice with real numbers, made honestly rather than by drift.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Clinical trial (the honest first choice)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: NCCN MDS v3.2026: clinical trial is the preferred listing after HMA failure
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: After the monthly injections stop working, no approved drug has beaten the honest, hard numbers - which is exactly why a trial is the first-listed option, not the last resort.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Allogeneic transplant after HMA failure (still fit)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: transplant-related mortality is higher after HMA failure than in first-line consolidation
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If a transplant is still medically realistic, it is the one path after treatment failure that can still aim for cure - harder now than it would have been earlier.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Conventional-care salvage (low-intensity)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: no standard of care exists after HMA failure
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Gentle treatment aimed at slowing things and supporting counts. It is honest to say it has not been shown to lengthen life after the injections fail.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Full attention on comfort, energy, and time - with transfusions continued or gently wound down according to your goals.
drugs: Palliative care partnership, transfusion support per goals

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date; every 'confirm' lives in the manifest staleness list.

Transfusion independence is a quality-of-life endpoint, not a survival claim - every lower-risk rung carries the label and is excluded from survival ranking by the engine, not by editorial discipline.

The VERONA negative renders at face value: better marrow responses (composite CR 48.8% vs 27.7% real-world) did NOT become longer survival (HR 0.908, p=0.38), and the aza+ven card ranks at or below azacitidine alone BEC…
Cross-trial comparison caveat: arms on one menu were earned in different trials with different populations; the horizon chip on each card is load-bearing.
The rec-state medians are COHORT numbers (Prebet), not arm-specific promises - two cards share 5.6 months on purpose and the cards say so.
Reroutes never rank: blasts >=20% is AML (its trainer is linked), and MDS/MPN overlap is a different family that the pivotal MDS trials excluded by protocol (its queued registry row is linked).
Registry wins for status; the peer-reviewed paper wins for numbers; both are logged.
gates: Bone marrow blasts >=20% is AML by definition (WHO-HAEM5) - a different disease with its own trainer
Proliferative/overlap features (sustained monocytosis, dysplastic-plus-proliferative marrow) belong to the MDS/MPN overlap family - CMML and relatives, a separate WHO-HAEM5 family
IPSS-M (or IPSS-R) risk group must be resulted before therapy ranking
care: Community oncology is the honest home of MDS care
Molecular panel access (IPSS-M is a send-out, not a relocation)
FACT-accredited transplant program + the 90-day donor clock

surveillance.phase: lower-risk on observation or a working anemia rung
surveillance.cadence: CBC and transfusion log every 1-3 months; marrow only for count deterioration or new cytopenias
CBC per cycle; IWG response assessment at cycle 4-6; donor-search clock runs in parallel for the fit
